question.text: Comparing option strategy risk profiles across derivative markets, which statement is universally true?

answer.text: Option buyers have loss limited to premium paid; long calls have potentially unlimited profit while long puts have substantial but bounded profit (underlying can only fall to zero); option sellers have limited premium income with unlimited/substantial loss; defined-risk spreads cap both profit and loss
Option strategies have different structural risk profiles in different markets
All option strategies have unlimited risk and unlimited reward
Risk profiles depend on the exchange, not the strategy structure

explanation.text: The Logic: The Equity Derivatives and Currency Derivatives workbooks set out the same risk profiles for option positions: (1) Long option: loss limited to premium paid; long calls have potentially unlimited profit and long puts have substantial (but bounded — underlying can only fall to zero) profit. (2) Short naked option: profit limited to premium received, loss unlimited (calls) or substantial (puts). (3) Spreads: limited profit and limited loss on both sides. The Trap: Long put profit is not literally unlimited — it is capped because the underlying cannot go below zero. Naked calls carry unlimited loss; naked puts carry substantial but bounded loss for the same reason. Risk depends on strategy structure, not on the exchange. Note: Premium levels and Greeks differ across underlyings, but the structural payoff for a given strategy (long option / short option / spread) is consistent across the equity and currency segments covered in the assigned source pages.
